name: Qianqian Jingting (千千静听, TTPlayer)
blurb: China's favorite free PC music player of the 2000s, known for synced lyrics and skins
title: What Was Qianqian Jingting (千千静听)? China's TTPlayer
description: Qianqian Jingting (千千静听, TTPlayer) was a free Windows music player hugely popular in 2000s China. Baidu bought it in 2006 and renamed it Baidu Music in 2013.
answer: Qianqian Jingting (千千静听, English name TTPlayer) was a free Windows music player that most Chinese PC users of the 2000s had installed, a local equivalent of Winamp. It was small and fast, played almost any audio format, fetched lyrics automatically and scrolled them line by line, and could be reskinned endlessly. Baidu bought it in July 2006 and renamed it Baidu Music in July 2013, which ended the original player; Baidu Music in turn became Qianqian Music in 2018.

body: In the years when people downloaded MP3s and kept them on their hard drives, Qianqian Jingting was standard software on a new PC. The installer was small, it launched quickly and handled the common audio formats.

ul: Lyrics: it searched a lyrics server automatically and highlighted each line in time with the song, and could float lyrics across the desktop
Skins: the player, playlist and lyrics windows snapped together, and fans made a huge range of skins
Mini mode and global hotkeys, so it stayed out of the way while gaming or doing homework
Tag editing to fix song titles and artist names

body: It was first called "MP3 Suishenting" (MP3 Walkman). The later name, roughly "listen quietly to thousands", echoes the Cantonese song Qianqian Que Ge (千千阙歌), which its developer liked.

body: The rename was part of Baidu's shift from local playback to an online music service. As licensed streaming apps such as QQ Music and NetEase Cloud Music took over, people stopped collecting MP3 files, and local players in general faded.

The original Qianqian Jingting has had no official update since 2013. Fans still keep old versions and skins online, but those are unofficial. The Qianqian Music name lives on in an online music service, which is a different product from the old player.

faq.a: Not officially. It was replaced by Baidu Music in 2013 and has not been updated since. Copies online come from unofficial sources.

faq.q: Are Qianqian Jingting and Qianqian Music the same thing?
faq.a: No. Qianqian Music is what Baidu Music was renamed in 2018, borrowing the old player's name, but it is an online music service rather than the original desktop player.
Very much: a lightweight, skinnable desktop player for local music files. Its built-in synced lyrics were the feature Chinese users loved most.
